_note: Fully synthetic call for --mock mode. Invented people and companies. spk_1 is the prospect (answers the phone). spk_2 is the rep.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Orsolo Freight, this is Jordan.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Hi Jordan, this is Sam from Vantrellis. Thanks for making time today. Is it okay if I record this call for my notes?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Sure, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Great. I was hoping to spend about twenty minutes learning how your team schedules drivers today, then show you one thing if it fits. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Yeah. I've got a hard stop at the half hour though.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Understood. So how are you building the weekly driver schedule right now?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Honestly it's a big spreadsheet. Our dispatcher rebuilds it every Friday and it takes her most of the afternoon. And then something changes Monday and she's redoing it.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Most of the afternoon every Friday. What happens when it changes on Monday?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: We end up calling drivers one by one. Last month we missed two pickups because the update didn't reach the driver in time. That cost us a customer, actually.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: You lost a customer over it? How big was that account?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: About sixty thousand a year. It wasn't just the missed pickups, but that was the last straw for them.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: That's painful. So if I'm hearing you right, the Friday rebuild eats your dispatcher's afternoon, the Monday changes don't reach drivers fast enough, and that already cost you a sixty thousand dollar account. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Yeah, that's about right.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Okay. What we do is let the dispatcher change the schedule in one place, and every driver gets the update on their phone within a minute, with a confirm button. So she would see who has confirmed and who hasn't.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Okay. What does something like that cost?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: For a fleet your size it's forty-eight hundred dollars a month.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Hmm. That's more than I expected. We're a small team.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: What were you expecting it to be?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: I don't know, maybe half that? I'd have to take this to our COO anyway.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: That makes sense. Besides the price, what would your COO need to see to say yes?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Probably proof it works with our dispatch software. And that the drivers will actually use it.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Would it help if we set up a thirty minute call with your COO next week where I show it running with your dispatch software?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Maybe. Just send me something I can forward first.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: I can do that. Can we also put a time on the calendar now, say Tuesday at ten, so it doesn't slip?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Tuesday at ten could work. Send the invite.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Will do. Thanks Jordan, talk Tuesday.
